correctness.rationale: Gnomonic Jacobian maps endpoints exactly to the normalized planar 2D Cauchy density. The single segment directional coarea integral factors into elementary half-line Cauchy integrals, yielding \(J=1/(2\pi^2sc)\) with correct endpoint order factor 2. The transverse two-line offset-to-intersection Jacobian gives \(|\sin(\alpha-\beta)|\). Absolutely/uniformly convergent Fourier expansions evaluate the angular double integral exactly; integration and the odd-reciprocal-square sum yield the correct subprobability mass. The continuous pole/equator limits and strict monotonicity follow by elementary calculus. The packaged standalone checker numerically evaluates pre-Fourier integrals and independently simulates 600000 samples; finite diagnostics support but do not replace the proof. Normalization, quantifiers and sampling convention were independently reconstructed.

value.rationale: The spatial location law is a natural refinement of the classical probability that two random geodesic segments cross. It determines pole-to-equator crossing localization and exact local crossing intensity for any finite family of independent arcs, quantities not determined by scalar crossing probabilities or single-segment midpoint distributions. The logarithmic radial profile is nontrivial and is derived by exact coarea plus Fourier convolution, useful for geometric network intensity and simulation benchmarks.
